name: Shankara Buildpro Ltd
title: Shankara Buildpro Ltd - 544517 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 6,826 crore and EBITDA margin reached 3.35%; FY27 guided to about 20% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Shankara Buildpro reported its first full year as a separately listed entity after the 1-1 demerger from Shankara Building Products, with FY26 revenue of INR 6,826 crore (+30% YoY) and Q4 revenue of INR 1,996 crore (+28% YoY, +20% QoQ). Steel volume crossed 1 million tonnes (10.16 lakh tonnes) and EBITDA rose 51% to INR 228 crore, with margin up 47 bps to 3.35%. PAT was INR 128 crore (+64%), with Q4 PAT of INR 42 crore (+42% YoY, +66% QoQ). Management flagged early-Q1 FY27 demand softness from the sharp price increases in March, tile supply disruption at Morbi, and a shortage of coated steel products, while guiding to about 20% growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.05% in Q4 FY25 and 3.30% in Q3 FY26
+64% YoY; includes one-time INR 2.61 crore labour code provision

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: FY26 steel volume reached 10.16 lakh tonnes (+32% YoY) and Q4 volume was 2.89 lakh tonnes (+19% YoY, +11% QoQ). Steel tubes and pipes were about 6.9-7 lakh tonnes in FY26. Management puts steel EBITDA margin at about 3%.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: FY26 non-steel revenue was INR 606 crore (+2% YoY) and Q4 was INR 161 crore. Non-steel EBITDA margin is about 6.5%, and non-steel is just under 10% of revenue. E-commerce revenue was INR 22 crore (+322% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tonnes; FY28 target 1.4 million tonnes; 2 million tonnes by FY31. Steel volume growth of about 20% guided for FY27 and similar for FY28.
Steel tubes and pipes to rise from about 6.9-7 lakh tonnes in FY26 to 1 million tonnes in about three years (about 18-20% growth in FY27).
Non-steel revenue target INR 750 crore in FY27 (+25%) and INR 925 crore in FY28. Non-steel share to reach 15-20% over 4-5 years (later framed as 15-16% in 3-5 years).
EBITDA margin guided at about 3.3-3.5% for FY27; medium-term aspiration of about 4%, now expected by FY29 at the latest, with management saying it could be ASAP.

E-commerce revenue target INR 35 crore in FY27 and INR 50 crore in FY28. Fulfilment centres/stores: 7-10 in FY27 (3 already opened), then 4-5 per year from FY28. Capex INR 15-20 crore for FY27 expansion; FY27 rent about INR 10 crore.
capex_capacity: Plan to add 7-10 fulfilment centres/stores in FY27, with 3 already opened: Vasai (Maharashtra, steel tubes only), Thrissur (Kerala, steel) and Bengaluru (non-steel).
FY27 capex for the new fulfilment centres estimated at INR 15-20 crore.

Around 16 of the roughly 95-96 retail counters are leased from sister company Shankara Building Products; most fulfilment centres and warehouses are owned by it. Shankara Buildpro does not own any stores.

Expansion is planned within existing geographies for now; no move into new states is contemplated. Growth to date has come from southern territories and newer areas such as Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
demand_pricing: Sharp price increases in March 2026 across tiles, pipes and some steel are expected to weigh on April-June demand; some postponement of purchases is occurring. Management says normalisation is expected over the year.

Morbi tile output was badly hit from March due to gas shortages. Prices rose 10-15%, and supply is expected to normalise by June at higher prices. Coated steel products also faced shortages in March-May, now easing.

Management estimates Q1 FY27 volumes are about 10-15% above Q1 FY26, with about 50% of the quarter elapsed. It expects Q2 to be the stronger quarter, aided by monsoon-season recovery and festive demand.

Steel price volatility: hot-rolled coil fell in Q2-Q3 FY26 and rose sharply in Q4. Safeguard duties have firmed domestic prices. Inventory gain in Q4 was about INR 15 crore; Q1 gains are expected to largely square off as prices plateau in May-June.

Retail accounts for about 50% of steel sales. Roughly 50% of business comes from metros and about 50% from Tier-2 to rural areas. Top customers account for about 1% of revenue, so client concentration is low.

Management says it is pushing non-steel growth through CPVC/PVC (small base), UPVC roofing (imports from China under its Ganga brand), and recovery in CP, sanitaryware and tiles. Plastic pipe industry volumes fell in FY26, and Jal Jeevan disbursement was about one-third of budget.
Competition: larger players dump into metro dealer channels, but management says its decentralised retail model keeps it relatively shielded. Quick commerce is viewed as an opportunity, not a threat.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of March price hikes on demand and April/May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says demand is hit to a small extent in April-June with some purchase postponement, but it expects the year to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How will 1.2 million tonnes be achieved given Q1 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that the 1.2 million tonnes target covers all steel, not just tubes (about 7 lakh tonnes today). It expects Q1 to be slightly slow and Q2 to lead.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the 25% non-steel growth to INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is expected from CPVC/PVC (small base), UPVC roofing with Chinese imports under the Ganga brand, and recovery in CP, sanitaryware and tiles.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin improvement limited to 3.3-3.5% in FY27 despite operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the guidance conservative and said the aspiration is for the upper end of the range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 inventory gain and the one-off costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inventory gain was about INR 15 crore, offset by about INR 16 crore of one-offs: INR 2.5 crore demerger cost, INR 2.5 crore additional rent and INR 11 crore bad debt provision, all in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the FY27 revenue growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of about 20% in FY27; EBITDA margin of about 3.3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel margin versus non-steel margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said non-steel EBITDA margin is about 6.5% and steel about 3%.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 demand softness from price hikes; Q2 must carry the volume target. Monitor June recovery and Morbi tile supply normalisation.
Steel price volatility and inventory gains or losses; Q1 gains expected to square off.
Non-steel growth of 25% against a flat FY26 (+2%) and weak tile, plastic pipe and Jal Jeevan demand. Management's plan rests on new categories (CPVC/PVC, UPVC roofing).
Related-party dependence: most fulfilment centres and warehouses and about 16 of 95-96 counters are owned by sister company Shankara Building Products.
Competitive pressure from large new-age and corporate distributors, and the proposed IPO of a large OP business.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term volume and margin trajectory but cautious on near-term demand, with management openly flagging a Q1 FY27 slowdown from price hikes and supply disruptions. Answers on non-steel growth and margin were less specific, and some questions (such as on the sister company) were deferred.
key_quotes: So, I would say yes, the flat products would grow at a slightly faster pace, but steel tubes will not be way behind.
Definitely, in the two to three years time frame, so sort of a medium-term outlook.
I don't think it's a competition. It's more of a new vertical in the future.
Definitely, the kind of sharp increases of prices across the board in whether it's tiles, whether it's partly in steel, whether it's other products is definitely impacting demand to a small extent.

adds.what: 7-10 fulfilment centres/stores in FY27 (3 already opened: Vasai, Thrissur, Bengaluru)
Steel tubes and pipes capacity to reach 1 million tonnes/yr from ~6.9-7 lakh tonnes in about three years

growth.why: Management guides about 20% FY27 revenue growth with steel volume of 1.2 Mt (~20%) and non-steel revenue of INR 750 crore (+25%), backed mainly by stated demand, new fulfilment centres (7-10 in FY27, capex INR 15-20 crore) and non-steel push, but without specific capacity or order numbers for the steel volume; Q1 FY27 volumes seen only 10-15% above prior year amid price-hike demand softness.
